ca_creek_slab.blurb: Creek Slab is a big pale boulder standing in a streambed in the Mary Fork Boulders, part of the Redding area of Northeast California. It has eight problems, running from V0 up to V5, with two each at V4 and V5, so there is something for newer boulderers and a few for stronger ones. The slab itself gives a handful of friendly moderate lines over a flat landing, and a cave at the back offers a shady spot to rest between goes. It sits right by the water, so expect a short stroll from the trail.

ca_tomb_of_dracula.blurb: Tomb of Dracula is a boulder in the Central Atlantis cluster, in the Tramway area of the San Jacinto Mountains above Idyllwild. Its shape is a giant shard that forms a cave with an entrance at each end, and it stays in shade through most of the day. There are eight problems, graded from VB through V5, with a couple at V0 and the rest spread evenly across the middle and upper grades. Central Atlantis packs several boulders close together, so a session here can easily combine this one with its neighbours.

ca_ragnarok_dome.blurb: Ragnarok Dome stands among the small domes of the 31 Milestone Tract, a short drive off Highway 50 near Kyburz in the Lake Tahoe region. It rises to about 90 feet, taller than its neighbours, and is recognizable by a long splitter lieback corner. There are eight routes, four sport and four trad, ranging from a 5.6 up to 5.11, with most clustered at 5.10. A canopy of trees shades the tract, which makes it a handy fallback when the neighbouring open slabs get too hot. Bring a rack for the gear lines.

ca_cobblestone_wall.blurb: Cobblestone Wall is a small cliff in Marin County, reached from the Mickey's Beach and Kim's Gym side of the coast. It has eight routes, four bolted and four on gear, with grades from 5.10 up to 5.13 and the bulk at 5.11. A handful of the lines are multipitch. Traffic is light, so cracks can be overgrown at certain times of year, and the rock is best left a day or two after heavy rain before you visit. It makes a good option for a trad day close to the Bay Area.

ca_captains_boulder_the.blurb: The Captains Boulder is one of the volcanic breccia blocks at Miniholland, a bouldering area. The rock is covered in pockets from finger size up to fist size. One side is short and overhanging, the other tall and steep. It has eight problems, from VB to V3, with three at V3. Landings are mostly good but a few are tight, so bring pads and a spotter. The boulder lies uphill from the first boulder, and several smaller blocks below it hold easier lines.

ca_princess_slab_and_dark_helmet.blurb: Princess Slab and Dark Helmet make up the first section of Dark Crown, a dome on the Kern Plateau above Rodeo Flat in the southern Sierra, at roughly 7,900 feet. It holds eight routes, four bolted and four trad, with most of the sport lines at 5.10 and the gear routes running from 5.8 to 5.11. A comfortable ledge sits beneath the Dark Helmet line, handy for gearing up. Morning here is shaded and trees take over later. Bring a trad rack for the gear lines.

ca_atf_boulder.blurb: ATF Boulder is a single boulder on Mount Tamalpais in Marin County, sitting above the road a little under a mile beyond the Rock Springs lot. It has eight problems graded from V2 to V6. Five of them fall at V4 and V5, with one V6 at the top, so it suits climbers who have already moved beyond the first few grades of bouldering.
